Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency spike impacting live inference (p95/p99 regressions)

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a sharp increase in inference latency around 15:50 PDT. p95 has moved from ~120ms to ~1.2s and p99 is spiking above 3s. Our production traffic is hitting increased error rates (5xx) and timeouts. This is affecting several customer-facing features — we’ve already started throttling calls to reduce user impact.

Can you escalate this to your ops/on-call immediately? We need a public status page entry and an ETA for mitigation. Attaching a quick flamegraph + traces screenshot for the last 20 minutes.

Thanks — this is high priority for us.

Emily Chen
Site Reliability Engineer, Gridline, Inc.

Subject: Re: URGENT: Gridline live calls — p95/p99 spike, customer escalation (see below)

I’ve taken the on-call. Quick findings so far:
- Initial metrics show a sudden increase in token-generation latency across a subset of hosted-api nodes in us-west-2.
- Error-rate bump correlates with a specific model revision (rev 2027-07-29-rc3) under long-context (>2048 tokens) traffic.
- No infra-scale events (hosts healthy), kernel-level telemetry looks normal.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Post initial status (draft below) and mark SEV2 while we confirm scope.
2) Roll back traffic from rev 2027-07-29-rc3 to previous stable revision for affected customers (canary first).
3) Enable emergency routing to our dedicated pool for Gridline if rollback not feasible.

Draft status page blurb (please review, we need customer-facing language):
"We are investigating elevated request latency affecting a subset of Hosted API customers in the us-west-2 region. Our engineering teams are actively diagnosing root cause and working on mitigation. Some customers may experience increased response times or transient errors. We will post updates as we have more information."

Requesting approval to post and start rollback canary.

— Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for raising this quickly — we’ll keep you in the loop.

— Aditya
